entries.proposition: The study was informed by a regulator innovation meeting and is described as the largest dataset for motor, cognitive and behavioural measures in this disorder.
entries.snippet: The CANDID study is a large observational CDD trial conducted to industry quality standards and informed by a Critical Path Innovation Meeting with the US Food and Drug Administration in 2021.

entries.proposition: Gross motor 88-item scores were at floor for crawling, standing and walking up to age 12 and the instrument was discontinued at later visits.
entries.snippet: Up to age 12 years, most of the GMFM scores were at floor for the crawling, standing, and walking GMFM levels.

entries.proposition: The instrument had operational limits: a refused task scores zero and later tasks are not evaluated.
entries.snippet: For example, refusal to perform a task results in a “0” score, and subsequent tasks are not evaluated, even if the child can often perform them.

entries.proposition: Bayley-4 growth scale values showed no floor or ceiling but scores stayed in the same range across age groups.
entries.snippet: Analyses of raw scores and GSVs showed no floor or ceiling effects. However, scores remained within the same range across age groups, indicating limited skills development but no regression

entries.proposition: Vineland-3 written, domestic and community subdomains showed floor effects; eight others had usable granularity.
entries.snippet: The most impacted subdomains were written, domestic, and community, all of which showed floor effects.

entries.proposition: Growth scale values are not age-normed and reflect raw developmental progress, so they suit monitoring change over time or after treatment.
entries.snippet: Unlike scaled or composite scores, GSVs are not age‐normed, meaning they reflect raw developmental progress rather than a comparison to age‐matched peers.

entries.proposition: No regression was seen in Vineland, Bayley or quality-of-life scores with age in this cross-sectional cohort; this must be confirmed longitudinally.
entries.snippet: This observation, however, will need to be confirmed with subsequent longitudinal data over the planned 3 years.

entries.proposition: Seizure counts are very high: median 25 to 100 per 28 days across age groups; six patients seizure-free, none before 3 years.
entries.snippet: The median seizure count ranged from 25 to 100 seizures within 28 days, corresponding to 1–5 daily.

entries.proposition: Seizure diaries were available for 82 of 111 patients.
entries.snippet: Seizure diaries from 82 patients were available

entries.proposition: Quality-of-life scores are caregiver-reported and the independence domain was lowest.
entries.snippet: The QI‐Disability questionnaire revealed a significant impact on overall QOL, especially in the independence component

entries.proposition: Supplement Table S3: gross motor 88-item scale judged unsuitable for trials; Bayley-4, Vineland-3 and other scales judged suitable at baseline.
entries.snippet: Floor effects were observed in all age groups for Crawling, Standing and Walking dimensions, more specifically for the youngest age group where 62-95% of the participants were at floor

entries.proposition: Supplement Table S3: a cerebral visual impairment range scale showed clear impairment and was judged an exploratory tool.
entries.snippet: Mean scores around 40% (i.e. clear CVI). High inter-subject variability. Exploratory tool.

entries.proposition: A seizure honeymoon at 1 or 2 years does not usually coincide with developmental improvement.
entries.snippet: Many children experience a seizure “honeymoon” period at 1 or 2 years of age, which typically lasts 2–18 months and does not usually coincide with development improvement.

entries.proposition: The study is funded by a precompetitive consortium of seven companies.
entries.snippet: This work was funded by the CANDID precompetitive consortium (i.e., CANDID partners)

entries.proposition: Cerebral visual impairment severity was not considered when interpreting motor or Bayley scores, and 26 percent of seizure diaries were missing after a year.
entries.snippet: We acknowledge that CVI severity was not considered when interpreting GMFM or Bayley‐4 scores.

entries.proposition: Fig 1 (28-day seizure counts): medians about 48 (0-2 y), 97 (3-5 y), 69 (6-12 y), 26 (13+ y) with outliers to 530 and interquartile ranges of 20 to over 100.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Boxplot of seizure count per 28 days by age group: medians about 48, 97, 69 and 26; interquartile boxes about 30-98, 22-120, 27-152 and 13-64; outliers up to about 530 in 3-5 years and 360 in 13+ years.

entries.proposition: Fig 2 (Vineland growth scale values by chronological age): eleven subdomain panels with individual points and fitted lines; written, domestic and community lie near the bottom of the scale and most others rise slowly with age.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Eleven panels (receptive and expressive language, written, personal care, domestic, community, interpersonal relationship, play and leisure, coping skills, fine motor, gross motor) with GSV about 0-160 on the y axis against chronological age 0-28 years; fitted blue lines rise gently in receptive language, interpersonal, fine and gross motor and are near flat in written, domestic and community.

entries.proposition: NOT WWOX EVIDENCE (CDKL5 deficiency disorder, baseline outcome-measure study). Table S3 reports 62 to 95 percent of the youngest age group at floor for the gross-motor crawling, standing and walking dimensions and marks the gross motor, cerebral visual impairment range and caregiver severity-rating scale suitability as NO, NO and YES.
entries.snippet: more specifically for the youngest age group where 62-95% of the participants were at floor
